_about.what: Morale and rest (the grand campaign). Every corps carries its morale, 0 to 1, beside its strength and its rest. Morale rises with victories, on home soil, with friends close by and with a quiet month out of the line; it falls with defeats, heavy losses, being cut off, going unpaid and standing alone in front of the enemy. A corps in good heart hits harder and holds together longer; a shaken one does neither.
_about.rule: Only the grand campaign keeps morale. A historical scenario has none: its corps fight exactly as they always did, and so its wars come out as they did before this rule was written.
_about.start: The morale a corps begins the war with, or is raised with.
_about.level: Where morale settles when nothing is happening to it, and 'drift', the share of the way back it goes each month. Because the mood settles by a share each month, what a corps gains every month adds up to a level and no further: 0.03 a month for home soil is worth 0.12 in the end, at a drift of 0.25.
_about.battle: What one battle does to the morale of the corps that fought it. 'won' and 'decisive' (odds of 2 to 1 or better) for attackers who carry the ground, 'repulsed' and 'thrown' (odds under 0.8 to 1) for attackers who do not; 'held' for defenders who keep their ground, 'lost' and 'routed' (2 to 1 or better against them) for defenders driven off it. 'bloody' is added for a corps that lost 'bloodyAt' of its men or more in the one fight. 'capital' is for the corps that take an enemy's capital, and 'capitalLost' is what every corps of a nation feels the day its own capital falls.
_about.month: The monthly reckoning, at the start of a nation's month. 'home': on its own country's soil. 'beside': other friendly corps in the same province. 'near': friendly corps in a province next door. 'alone': no friend in the province or next door, and the enemy next door. 'rested': a whole month in supply without marching or fighting. 'cutOff': out of supply. 'unpaid': the treasury is empty (scaled by how deep the debt is). 'winter': a winter in the east without winter equipment. 'general': a general in command who rallies men.
_about.fight: 'span': the whole range morale is worth in battle, half of it either side of morale 0.5 (0.3 is from 15% weaker to 15% stronger). 'steady': how much faster a corps with no heart loses its cohesion in a fight, and how much slower one in good heart does (0.5 is from 25% faster to 25% slower).
_about.rested: What a whole month out of the line is worth besides morale: 'org' more rest recovered, and drafts arriving 'drafts' times as fast.
_about.words: What a level of morale is called: [from, name].
_about.restWords: What a level of rest (cohesion) is called: [from, name].
_about.why: The words for each reason, as the player reads them.

why.thrown: An attack thrown back with loss
why.alone: Alone in front of the enemy
why.rested: A quiet month out of the line
